c.tagline: Lakeside capital where volcanoes and history meet.

taxi.fareNote: Most taxis are unmetered; agree on the fare (in córdobas) with the driver before getting in. Only use officially registered taxis, identifiable by a red stripe on the license plate.

emergency.note: Tourist hotline 101 (Claro mobile). Response times can be slow; use only officially marked red-striped taxis.

avoid.reason: Caution around the Mercado Oriental and at night

hood_desc: Leafy, embassy-lined residential district with quiet streets, boutique guesthouses and upscale restaurants; suits first-time visitors, business travelers and couples wanting a calm, central base.
Managua's commercial heart around the Metrocentro mall with malls, banks and chain hotels; suits business travelers and anyone wanting maximum convenience and easy transit access.
Modern strip of newer apartments, gyms, cafes and the Galerías Santo Domingo mall heading toward Masaya; suits digital nomads, families and longer-stay visitors with a car.

Historic district on the hill near Tiscapa Lagoon and Plaza Inter, home to the iconic pyramid-shaped former Intercontinental (now Crowne Plaza) and government buildings; suits history buffs and those wanting central, landmark-adjacent lodging.
Lakefront entertainment complex on Lake Xolotlán with restaurants, live music and weekend crowds; suits nightlife-focused travelers and short-stay visitors who don't mind noise.
lodging: Real InterContinental Managua at Metrocentro Mall

water.note: Avoid tap water; drink only bottled or purified water.

transit.pay: Fares on city buses are paid in cash (córdobas) directly to the driver or a fare collector on board; there is no rechargeable transit card. Taxis are typically negotiated up front since few are metered.
transit.hours: Buses run roughly 5:00am-10:00pm; limited service after dark, so taxis are the norm at night.
transit.note: Public buses are crowded, poorly marked and not recommended for tourists unfamiliar with the routes; licensed radio taxis are the practical option for visitors.

tip.r: Tipping isn't obligatory; 10% is appreciated at sit-down restaurants if a service charge isn't already included.
